List of notable events in music that took place in the year 1966.
*   [1966 in British music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_British_music "1966 in British music")  
*   [1966 in Japanese music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_Japanese_music "1966 in Japanese music")  
*   [1966 in Scandinavian music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_Scandinavian_music "1966 in Scandinavian music")

*   [1966 in country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_country_music "1966 in country music")  
*   [1966 in jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_jazz "1966 in jazz")

*   [January 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_8 "January 8") – The US TV show _[Shindig!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shindig! "Shindig!")_ is broadcast for the last time on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), with musical guests [the Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinks "The Kinks") and [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who"); 2 days earlier, the birthday of [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") is celebrated in the final Thursday episode of the series. The show premiered in September 1964 and from September 1965 aired twice a week, on Thursday and Saturday nights.  
*   [January 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_14 "January 14") – Young English singer David Jones changes his last name to [Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") to avoid being confused with [Davy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davy_Jones_(actor) "Davy Jones (actor)") of [the Monkees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monkees "The Monkees").  
*   [January 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_17 "January 17") – [Simon & Garfunkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Garfunkel "Simon & Garfunkel") release the [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album")_[Sounds of Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounds\_of\_Silence\_(album) "Sounds of Silence (album)")_ in the US.  

*   [February 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_2 "February 2") – The first edition of _[Go-Set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go-Set "Go-Set")_ magazine is published in Melbourne, Australia. Founded by former [Monash University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monash_University "Monash University") students [Phillip Frazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillip_Frazer "Phillip Frazer") and Tony Schauble, the new weekly is the first independent periodical in Australia devoted entirely to popular music and youth culture. The inaugural 24-page issue has a cover feature on [Tom Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Jones_(singer) "Tom Jones (singer)"), stories on [The Groop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Groop "The Groop"), singer [Pat Carroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Carroll_(singer) "Pat Carroll (singer)") and DJ [Ken Sparkes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Sparkes "Ken Sparkes") and a feature on [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_(subculture) "Mod (subculture)") fashion by designer [Prue Acton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prue_Acton "Prue Acton").  
*   [February 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_6 "February 6") – [The Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Animals "The Animals") appear a fifth time on _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ed\_Sullivan\_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ to perform their iconic Vietnam-anthem hit "[We Gotta Get Out of this Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Gotta_Get_Out_of_this_Place "We Gotta Get Out of this Place")".  

*   [February 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_17 "February 17") – [Brian Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Wilson "Brian Wilson") starts recording "[Good Vibrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Vibrations "Good Vibrations")" with [The Wrecking Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wrecking_Crew_(music) "The Wrecking Crew (music)"), continuing for several months and marking a beginning to the famed _[Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smile\_(Beach\_Boys\_album) "Smile (Beach Boys album)")_ sessions.  
*   [February 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_19 "February 19") – [Jefferson Airplane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Airplane "Jefferson Airplane") and [Big Brother and the Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Brother_and_the_Holding_Company "Big Brother and the Holding Company") with [Janis Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janis_Joplin "Janis Joplin") perform at [the Fillmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fillmore "The Fillmore").  
*   [February 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_25 "February 25") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") release the single "[Shapes of Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapes_of_Things "Shapes of Things")"/"[Mister, You're a Better Man Than I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister,_You're_a_Better_Man_Than_I "Mister, You're a Better Man Than I")", heralding the dawn of the psychedelic era in British rock. "Shapes" will peak at No. 3 in the UK and No. 10 in Canada and the US, where it remains on the charts throughout the spring of 1966, making its final Hot 100 appearance mid-June.  

*   [March 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_4 "March 4") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") is quoted in the London _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening\_Standard "Evening Standard")_ newspaper as saying that "We're [more popular than Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_popular_than_Jesus "More popular than Jesus") now." In August, following publication of this remark in Datebook, there are Beatles protests and record burnings in the Southern US's [Bible Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_Belt "Bible Belt").  
*   [March 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_5 "March 5") – The 11th [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1966 "Eurovision Song Contest 1966") is staged in the [Villa Louvigny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Louvigny "Villa Louvigny"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City"). [Udo Jürgens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udo_J%C3%BCrgens "Udo Jürgens"), having represented [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest "Austria in the Eurovision Song Contest") in the last two contests (sixth in 1964; fourth in 1965), finally scores a first for the country, with _"[Merci, Chérie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merci,\_Ch%C3%A9rie "Merci, Chérie")"_, which he co-wrote.  

*   [March 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_6 "March 6") – In the UK, 5,000 fans of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") sign a petition urging British Prime minister [Harold Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Wilson "Harold Wilson") to reopen [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool")'s [Cavern Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavern_Club "Cavern Club").  
*   [March 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_14 "March 14") – [The Byrds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Byrds "The Byrds") release the psychedelic single "[Eight Miles High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight_Miles_High "Eight Miles High")" in the US. It is banned in several states due to allegations that the lyrics advocate drug use, yet reaches No.14 on the Billboard 100 charts.  

*   [March 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_15 "March 15") – The [8th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "8th Annual Grammy Awards") are held in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), hosted by [Jerry Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lewis "Jerry Lewis"). [Roger Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Miller "Roger Miller") wins the most awards with five. [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra")'s _[September of My Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September\_of\_My\_Years "September of My Years")_ wins [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), [Herb Alpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herb_Alpert "Herb Alpert")& the Tijuana Brass' version of "[A Taste of Honey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey_(song) "A Taste of Honey (song)")" wins [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Tony Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Bennett "Tony Bennett")'s version of "[The Shadow of Your Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shadow_of_Your_Smile "The Shadow of Your Smile")" wins [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"). [Tom Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Jones_(singer) "Tom Jones (singer)") wins [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist").  

*   [April](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April "April") – [Herb Alpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herb_Alpert "Herb Alpert")& the Tijuana Brass set a world record by placing five albums simultaneously on Billboard's Pop Album Chart, with four of them the Top 10. Their music outsells [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") by a margin of two-to-one – over 13 million recordings. They win 4 Grammys this year.  
*   [April 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_11 "April 11") – First public performance in the [Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera_House_(Lincoln_Center) "Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)") in New York City, of [Giacomo Puccini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Puccini "Giacomo Puccini")'s _[La fanciulla del West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_fanciulla\_del\_West "La fanciulla del West")_, though the official opening of the new opera house will not take place until September 16.  
*   [April 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_12 "April 12") – In Los Angeles, California, [Jan Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Berry "Jan Berry"), of [Jan and Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_and_Dean "Jan and Dean"), crashes his [Corvette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_Corvette "Chevrolet Corvette") into a truck that is parked on Whittier Boulevard. Berry slips into a two-month-long coma and suffers total physical paralysis for over a year as well as extensive brain damage.  

*   [April 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_23 "April 23") – For the first time since its January 18, 1964, issue, the _Billboard_[Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart fails to have an artist from the UK with a Top 10 single, ending a streak of 117 consecutive weeks.  
*   [May 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1 "May 1") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), [The Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") and [The Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who") perform at the _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_'s poll winners' show at the [Empire Pool (Wembley)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Arena "Wembley Arena") in London. This will be The Beatles' last conventional live concert in Britain. The show is videotaped for later broadcast but The Beatles' and The Stones' segments are omitted because of union conflicts.  
*   [May 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_6 "May 6") – The first issue of _[Džuboks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C5%BEuboks "Džuboks")_, the first [Yugoslav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFRY "SFRY") magazine dedicated to rock music and the first rock magazine in a [socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_state "Socialist state") country, is released.  

*   [May 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_7 "May 7") – The [Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stones "Rolling Stones") release "[Paint It, Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paint_It,_Black "Paint It, Black")" in the US (May 13 in the UK); this becomes the first number one hit single in the US and UK to feature a sitar (played by [Brian Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Jones "Brian Jones")).  
*   [May 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_16 "May 16") – Legendary album _[Pet Sounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet\_Sounds "Pet Sounds")_ by [The Beach Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beach_Boys "The Beach Boys") is released in the US.  
*   [May 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_17 "May 17") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") and the Hawks (later [The Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band "The Band")) perform at the Free Trade Hall, Manchester, UK. Dylan is booed by the audience because of his decision to tour with an electric band, the boos culminating in the famous "Judas" shout.  
*   [May 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_30 "May 30") – [Them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_(band) "Them (band)"), fronted by [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"), begin a three-week stint as the headliner act at the [Whisky a Go Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whisky_a_Go_Go "Whisky a Go Go") in Hollywood. On the last night June 18, they are joined on stage by that week's opening act [The Doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors "The Doors"). Van and [Jim Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Morrison "Jim Morrison") sing "[Gloria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_(Them_song) "Gloria (Them song)")" together.  

*   [June 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_6 "June 6") – 25-year-old Claudette Frady-Orbison, while motorcycle riding with her husband [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison"), is killed when her motorcycle is struck by a pickup truck in [Gallatin, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallatin,_Tennessee "Gallatin, Tennessee").  
*   [June 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_18 "June 18") – At a drunken gig at [The Queen's College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen's_College,_Oxford "The Queen's College, Oxford"), in England, bassist/producer [Paul Samwell-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Samwell-Smith "Paul Samwell-Smith") quits [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") and star session guitarist [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page") agrees to take over on bass.  
*   [June 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_20 "June 20") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan")'s album _[Blonde on Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blonde\_on\_Blonde "Blonde on Blonde")_ is released in the US.  
*   [June 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_27 "June 27") – [Frank Zappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Zappa "Frank Zappa") and [The Mothers of Invention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mothers_of_Invention "The Mothers of Invention")'s debut album, _[Freak Out!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freak\_Out! "Freak Out!")_, is released in the US. It is an initial failure, but gains a massive cult following in subsequent years.  

*   [July 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_2 "July 2") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") become the first musical group to perform at the [Nippon Budokan Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nippon_Budokan_Hall "Nippon Budokan Hall") in Tokyo. The performance ignites protests from local citizens who feel that it is inappropriate for a rock and roll band to play at Budokan.  
*   [July 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_29 "July 29") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") is injured in a motorcycle accident near his home in [Woodstock, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_New_York "Woodstock, New York"). He is not seen in public for over a year.  
*   [July 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_31 "July 31") – The "supergroup" [Cream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cream_(band) "Cream (band)"), a trio featuring [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton") (guitar), [Ginger Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginger_Baker "Ginger Baker") (drums) and [Jack Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Bruce "Jack Bruce") (bass guitar, lead vocals) performs its first official concert at the Windsor (UK) Jazz & Blues Festival.  
*   [August 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_1 "August 1") – "Midsummer Serenades: A Mozart Festival" is held – the first [Mostly Mozart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostly_Mozart "Mostly Mozart") Festival.  
*   [August 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_5 "August 5") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") release their album _[Revolver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver\_(Beatles\_album) "Revolver (Beatles album)")_ in the UK, expanding the year's psychedelic sound.  

*   [August 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_11 "August 11") – [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") holds a press conference in Chicago, Illinois, to apologize for his remarks the previous March. "I suppose if I had said television was more popular than Jesus, I would have gotten away with it. I'm sorry I opened my mouth. I'm not anti-God, anti-Christ, or anti-religion. I was not knocking it. I was not saying we are greater or better."  
*   [August 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_17 "August 17") – The [Moscow Radio Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Radio_Symphony_Orchestra "Moscow Radio Symphony Orchestra") becomes the first major overseas orchestra to perform at [The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Proms "The Proms").  
*   [August 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_24 "August 24") – American rock band [The Doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors "The Doors") record their [self-titled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors_(album) "The Doors (album)") debut album.  
*   [August 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_25 "August 25") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds")' lead guitarist [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck") is taken ill in San Francisco and [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), who has been playing bass, takes over on lead guitar for the band's concert at the [Carousel Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carousel_Ballroom "Carousel Ballroom").  
*   [August 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_29 "August 29")  

    *   [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") perform their last official concert at [Candlestick Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candlestick_Park "Candlestick Park") in San Francisco, California. The last number they play is [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard")'s "[Long Tall Sally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Tall_Sally "Long Tall Sally")".  
    *   NBC airs the last episode of _Hullabaloo_(the episode previously aired in April).
*   [September 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_12 "September 12") – The first episode of _[The Monkees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monkees\_(TV\_series) "The Monkees (TV series)")_ television series is broadcast on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") in the US.  
*   [September 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_16 "September 16")  
    *   The [Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera_House_(Lincoln_Center) "Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)") opens in New York City with the première of [Samuel Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Barber "Samuel Barber")'s opera _Antony and Cleopatra_. The opera is rejected by the critics.  
    *   [Eric Burdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Burdon "Eric Burdon") records a solo album after leaving [The Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Animals "The Animals") and appears on the show _[Ready, Steady, Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ready,\_Steady,\_Go "Ready, Steady, Go")_, singing "[Help Me Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_Me_Girl "Help Me Girl")", a UK #14 solo hit. Also on the show are [Otis Redding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Redding "Otis Redding") and [Chris Farlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Farlowe "Chris Farlowe").

*   [September 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_23 "September 23") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") debut their twin lead guitar lineup, featuring [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck") and [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall") in London, opening for [The Rolling Stones 1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones_1966_tours "The Rolling Stones 1966 tours") UK tour. Also on the bill are [Ike & Tina Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ike_&_Tina_Turner "Ike & Tina Turner"), [Peter Jay and the New Jaywalkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jay_and_the_Jaywalkers "Peter Jay and the Jaywalkers") and [Long John Baldry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_John_Baldry "Long John Baldry").  
*   [September 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_24 "September 24") – [Jimi Hendrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimi_Hendrix "Jimi Hendrix") arrives in London to record with producer/manager [Chas Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chas_Chandler "Chas Chandler").  
*   [October 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_8 "October 8") – [WOR-FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WOR-FM "WOR-FM") in New York City becomes the first [FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FM_broadcasting "FM broadcasting") rock music station, under the leadership of DJ [Murray The K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_The_K "Murray The K").  

*   [October 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_22 "October 22") – With their album _[The Supremes A' Go-Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Supremes\_A'\_Go-Go "The Supremes A' Go-Go")_, [The Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") become the first all-female group to reach number one on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200").  
*   [November 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_9 "November 9") – [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") meets [Yoko Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoko_Ono "Yoko Ono") when he attends a preview of her art exhibition at the [Indica Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indica_Gallery "Indica Gallery") in London.  
*   [November 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_15 "November 15") – Japanese band [The Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tigers_(Japanese_band) "The Tigers (Japanese band)") make their first television appearance, changing their name from "The Funnys" for the occasion.  
*   [November 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_24 "November 24") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") begin recording sessions for their _[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sgt.\_Pepper's\_Lonely\_Hearts\_Club\_Band "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band")_ album at [Abbey Road Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbey_Road_Studios "Abbey Road Studios") in London.

*   [1966 in jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_in_jazz "1966 in jazz")
texts.1:
*   [January 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_8 "January 8") – The US TV show _[Shindig!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shindig! "Shindig!")_ is broadcast for the last time on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), with musical guests [the Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinks "The Kinks") and [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who"); 2 days earlier, the birthday of [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") is celebrated in the final Thursday episode of the series. The show premiered in September 1964 and from September 1965 aired twice a week, on Thursday and Saturday nights.  
*   [January 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_14 "January 14") – Young English singer David Jones changes his last name to [Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") to avoid being confused with [Davy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davy_Jones_(actor) "Davy Jones (actor)") of [the Monkees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monkees "The Monkees").  
*   [January 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_17 "January 17") – [Simon & Garfunkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Garfunkel "Simon & Garfunkel") release the [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album")_[Sounds of Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounds\_of\_Silence\_(album) "Sounds of Silence (album)")_ in the US.
texts.2:
*   [February 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_2 "February 2") – The first edition of _[Go-Set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go-Set "Go-Set")_ magazine is published in Melbourne, Australia. Founded by former [Monash University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monash_University "Monash University") students [Phillip Frazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillip_Frazer "Phillip Frazer") and Tony Schauble, the new weekly is the first independent periodical in Australia devoted entirely to popular music and youth culture. The inaugural 24-page issue has a cover feature on [Tom Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Jones_(singer) "Tom Jones (singer)"), stories on [The Groop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Groop "The Groop"), singer [Pat Carroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Carroll_(singer) "Pat Carroll (singer)") and DJ [Ken Sparkes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Sparkes "Ken Sparkes") and a feature on [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_(subculture) "Mod (subculture)") fashion by designer [Prue Acton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prue_Acton "Prue Acton").  
*   [February 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_6 "February 6") – [The Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Animals "The Animals") appear a fifth time on _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ed\_Sullivan\_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ to perform their iconic Vietnam-anthem hit "[We Gotta Get Out of this Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Gotta_Get_Out_of_this_Place "We Gotta Get Out of this Place")".
texts.3:
*   [February 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_17 "February 17") – [Brian Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Wilson "Brian Wilson") starts recording "[Good Vibrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Vibrations "Good Vibrations")" with [The Wrecking Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wrecking_Crew_(music) "The Wrecking Crew (music)"), continuing for several months and marking a beginning to the famed _[Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smile\_(Beach\_Boys\_album) "Smile (Beach Boys album)")_ sessions.  
*   [February 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_19 "February 19") – [Jefferson Airplane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Airplane "Jefferson Airplane") and [Big Brother and the Holding Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Brother_and_the_Holding_Company "Big Brother and the Holding Company") with [Janis Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janis_Joplin "Janis Joplin") perform at [the Fillmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fillmore "The Fillmore").  
*   [February 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_25 "February 25") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") release the single "[Shapes of Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapes_of_Things "Shapes of Things")"/"[Mister, You're a Better Man Than I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister,_You're_a_Better_Man_Than_I "Mister, You're a Better Man Than I")", heralding the dawn of the psychedelic era in British rock. "Shapes" will peak at No. 3 in the UK and No. 10 in Canada and the US, where it remains on the charts throughout the spring of 1966, making its final Hot 100 appearance mid-June.
texts.4:
*   [March 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_4 "March 4") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") is quoted in the London _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening\_Standard "Evening Standard")_ newspaper as saying that "We're [more popular than Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_popular_than_Jesus "More popular than Jesus") now." In August, following publication of this remark in Datebook, there are Beatles protests and record burnings in the Southern US's [Bible Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_Belt "Bible Belt").  
*   [March 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_5 "March 5") – The 11th [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1966 "Eurovision Song Contest 1966") is staged in the [Villa Louvigny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Louvigny "Villa Louvigny"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City"). [Udo Jürgens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udo_J%C3%BCrgens "Udo Jürgens"), having represented [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest "Austria in the Eurovision Song Contest") in the last two contests (sixth in 1964; fourth in 1965), finally scores a first for the country, with _"[Merci, Chérie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merci,\_Ch%C3%A9rie "Merci, Chérie")"_, which he co-wrote.
texts.5:
*   [March 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_6 "March 6") – In the UK, 5,000 fans of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") sign a petition urging British Prime minister [Harold Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Wilson "Harold Wilson") to reopen [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool")'s [Cavern Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavern_Club "Cavern Club").  
*   [March 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_14 "March 14") – [The Byrds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Byrds "The Byrds") release the psychedelic single "[Eight Miles High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight_Miles_High "Eight Miles High")" in the US. It is banned in several states due to allegations that the lyrics advocate drug use, yet reaches No.14 on the Billboard 100 charts.
texts.6: *   [March 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_15 "March 15") – The [8th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "8th Annual Grammy Awards") are held in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), hosted by [Jerry Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lewis "Jerry Lewis"). [Roger Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Miller "Roger Miller") wins the most awards with five. [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra")'s _[September of My Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September\_of\_My\_Years "September of My Years")_ wins [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), [Herb Alpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herb_Alpert "Herb Alpert")& the Tijuana Brass' version of "[A Taste of Honey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey_(song) "A Taste of Honey (song)")" wins [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Tony Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Bennett "Tony Bennett")'s version of "[The Shadow of Your Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shadow_of_Your_Smile "The Shadow of Your Smile")" wins [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"). [Tom Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Jones_(singer) "Tom Jones (singer)") wins [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist").
texts.7:
*   [April](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April "April") – [Herb Alpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herb_Alpert "Herb Alpert")& the Tijuana Brass set a world record by placing five albums simultaneously on Billboard's Pop Album Chart, with four of them the Top 10. Their music outsells [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") by a margin of two-to-one – over 13 million recordings. They win 4 Grammys this year.  
*   [April 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_11 "April 11") – First public performance in the [Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera_House_(Lincoln_Center) "Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)") in New York City, of [Giacomo Puccini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Puccini "Giacomo Puccini")'s _[La fanciulla del West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_fanciulla\_del\_West "La fanciulla del West")_, though the official opening of the new opera house will not take place until September 16.  
*   [April 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_12 "April 12") – In Los Angeles, California, [Jan Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Berry "Jan Berry"), of [Jan and Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_and_Dean "Jan and Dean"), crashes his [Corvette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_Corvette "Chevrolet Corvette") into a truck that is parked on Whittier Boulevard. Berry slips into a two-month-long coma and suffers total physical paralysis for over a year as well as extensive brain damage.
texts.8:
*   [April 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_23 "April 23") – For the first time since its January 18, 1964, issue, the _Billboard_[Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart fails to have an artist from the UK with a Top 10 single, ending a streak of 117 consecutive weeks.  
*   [May 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1 "May 1") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), [The Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") and [The Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who") perform at the _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_'s poll winners' show at the [Empire Pool (Wembley)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Arena "Wembley Arena") in London. This will be The Beatles' last conventional live concert in Britain. The show is videotaped for later broadcast but The Beatles' and The Stones' segments are omitted because of union conflicts.  
*   [May 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_6 "May 6") – The first issue of _[Džuboks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C5%BEuboks "Džuboks")_, the first [Yugoslav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFRY "SFRY") magazine dedicated to rock music and the first rock magazine in a [socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_state "Socialist state") country, is released.
texts.9:
*   [May 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_7 "May 7") – The [Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stones "Rolling Stones") release "[Paint It, Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paint_It,_Black "Paint It, Black")" in the US (May 13 in the UK); this becomes the first number one hit single in the US and UK to feature a sitar (played by [Brian Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Jones "Brian Jones")).  
*   [May 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_16 "May 16") – Legendary album _[Pet Sounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet\_Sounds "Pet Sounds")_ by [The Beach Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beach_Boys "The Beach Boys") is released in the US.  
*   [May 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_17 "May 17") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") and the Hawks (later [The Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band "The Band")) perform at the Free Trade Hall, Manchester, UK. Dylan is booed by the audience because of his decision to tour with an electric band, the boos culminating in the famous "Judas" shout.  
*   [May 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_30 "May 30") – [Them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_(band) "Them (band)"), fronted by [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"), begin a three-week stint as the headliner act at the [Whisky a Go Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whisky_a_Go_Go "Whisky a Go Go") in Hollywood. On the last night June 18, they are joined on stage by that week's opening act [The Doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors "The Doors"). Van and [Jim Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Morrison "Jim Morrison") sing "[Gloria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_(Them_song) "Gloria (Them song)")" together.
texts.10:
*   [June 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_6 "June 6") – 25-year-old Claudette Frady-Orbison, while motorcycle riding with her husband [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison"), is killed when her motorcycle is struck by a pickup truck in [Gallatin, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallatin,_Tennessee "Gallatin, Tennessee").  
*   [June 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_18 "June 18") – At a drunken gig at [The Queen's College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen's_College,_Oxford "The Queen's College, Oxford"), in England, bassist/producer [Paul Samwell-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Samwell-Smith "Paul Samwell-Smith") quits [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") and star session guitarist [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page") agrees to take over on bass.  
*   [June 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_20 "June 20") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan")'s album _[Blonde on Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blonde\_on\_Blonde "Blonde on Blonde")_ is released in the US.  
*   [June 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_27 "June 27") – [Frank Zappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Zappa "Frank Zappa") and [The Mothers of Invention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mothers_of_Invention "The Mothers of Invention")'s debut album, _[Freak Out!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freak\_Out! "Freak Out!")_, is released in the US. It is an initial failure, but gains a massive cult following in subsequent years.
texts.11:
*   [July 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_2 "July 2") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") become the first musical group to perform at the [Nippon Budokan Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nippon_Budokan_Hall "Nippon Budokan Hall") in Tokyo. The performance ignites protests from local citizens who feel that it is inappropriate for a rock and roll band to play at Budokan.  
*   [July 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_29 "July 29") – [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") is injured in a motorcycle accident near his home in [Woodstock, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_New_York "Woodstock, New York"). He is not seen in public for over a year.  
*   [July 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_31 "July 31") – The "supergroup" [Cream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cream_(band) "Cream (band)"), a trio featuring [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton") (guitar), [Ginger Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginger_Baker "Ginger Baker") (drums) and [Jack Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Bruce "Jack Bruce") (bass guitar, lead vocals) performs its first official concert at the Windsor (UK) Jazz & Blues Festival.  
*   [August 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_1 "August 1") – "Midsummer Serenades: A Mozart Festival" is held – the first [Mostly Mozart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostly_Mozart "Mostly Mozart") Festival.  
*   [August 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_5 "August 5") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") release their album _[Revolver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver\_(Beatles\_album) "Revolver (Beatles album)")_ in the UK, expanding the year's psychedelic sound.
texts.12:
*   [August 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_11 "August 11") – [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") holds a press conference in Chicago, Illinois, to apologize for his remarks the previous March. "I suppose if I had said television was more popular than Jesus, I would have gotten away with it. I'm sorry I opened my mouth. I'm not anti-God, anti-Christ, or anti-religion. I was not knocking it. I was not saying we are greater or better."  
*   [August 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_17 "August 17") – The [Moscow Radio Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Radio_Symphony_Orchestra "Moscow Radio Symphony Orchestra") becomes the first major overseas orchestra to perform at [The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Proms "The Proms").  
*   [August 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_24 "August 24") – American rock band [The Doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors "The Doors") record their [self-titled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors_(album) "The Doors (album)") debut album.  
*   [August 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_25 "August 25") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds")' lead guitarist [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck") is taken ill in San Francisco and [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), who has been playing bass, takes over on lead guitar for the band's concert at the [Carousel Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carousel_Ballroom "Carousel Ballroom").  
*   [August 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_29 "August 29")
texts.13:
*   [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") perform their last official concert at [Candlestick Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candlestick_Park "Candlestick Park") in San Francisco, California. The last number they play is [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard")'s "[Long Tall Sally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Tall_Sally "Long Tall Sally")".  
    *   NBC airs the last episode of _Hullabaloo_(the episode previously aired in April).
*   [September 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_12 "September 12") – The first episode of _[The Monkees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monkees\_(TV\_series) "The Monkees (TV series)")_ television series is broadcast on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") in the US.  
*   [September 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_16 "September 16")  
    *   The [Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera_House_(Lincoln_Center) "Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)") opens in New York City with the première of [Samuel Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Barber "Samuel Barber")'s opera _Antony and Cleopatra_. The opera is rejected by the critics.  
    *   [Eric Burdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Burdon "Eric Burdon") records a solo album after leaving [The Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Animals "The Animals") and appears on the show _[Ready, Steady, Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ready,\_Steady,\_Go "Ready, Steady, Go")_, singing "[Help Me Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_Me_Girl "Help Me Girl")", a UK #14 solo hit. Also on the show are [Otis Redding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Redding "Otis Redding") and [Chris Farlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Farlowe "Chris Farlowe").
texts.14:
*   [September 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_23 "September 23") – [The Yardbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yardbirds "The Yardbirds") debut their twin lead guitar lineup, featuring [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck") and [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall") in London, opening for [The Rolling Stones 1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones_1966_tours "The Rolling Stones 1966 tours") UK tour. Also on the bill are [Ike & Tina Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ike_&_Tina_Turner "Ike & Tina Turner"), [Peter Jay and the New Jaywalkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jay_and_the_Jaywalkers "Peter Jay and the Jaywalkers") and [Long John Baldry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_John_Baldry "Long John Baldry").  
*   [September 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_24 "September 24") – [Jimi Hendrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimi_Hendrix "Jimi Hendrix") arrives in London to record with producer/manager [Chas Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chas_Chandler "Chas Chandler").  
*   [October 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_8 "October 8") – [WOR-FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WOR-FM "WOR-FM") in New York City becomes the first [FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FM_broadcasting "FM broadcasting") rock music station, under the leadership of DJ [Murray The K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_The_K "Murray The K").
texts.15:
*   [October 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_22 "October 22") – With their album _[The Supremes A' Go-Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Supremes\_A'\_Go-Go "The Supremes A' Go-Go")_, [The Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") become the first all-female group to reach number one on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200").  
*   [November 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_9 "November 9") – [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") meets [Yoko Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoko_Ono "Yoko Ono") when he attends a preview of her art exhibition at the [Indica Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indica_Gallery "Indica Gallery") in London.  
*   [November 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_15 "November 15") – Japanese band [The Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tigers_(Japanese_band) "The Tigers (Japanese band)") make their first television appearance, changing their name from "The Funnys" for the occasion.  
*   [November 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_24 "November 24") – [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") begin recording sessions for their _[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sgt.\_Pepper's\_Lonely\_Hearts\_Club\_Band "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band")_ album at [Abbey Road Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbey_Road_Studios "Abbey Road Studios") in London.

**Bezimeni** (trans. _The Nameless Ones_) were a [Croatian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and [Yugoslav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFRY "SFRY")[rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band formed in [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb "Zagreb") in 1961, notable as one of the pioneers of the [Yugoslav rock scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_rock_scene "Yugoslav rock scene"). In the early 1960s, the band gained popularity with their live performances on which they covered [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_America "United States of America")[rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") hits. The group disbanded in 1964, reuniting 36 years later for a live performance, recording several of their 1960s songs for the first time.
Bezimeni were formed in 1961 by [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb "Zagreb") high school students Janko Mlinarić "Truli" (vocals, bass guitar), Slaven Rački (guitar), Željko Margetić "Marga" (guitar), Mahmud Ismailovski "Mamut" (tenor saxophone) and Mario Škrinjarić (drums).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) The five made an agreement to form the band during a school excursion to [Poreč](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pore%C4%8D "Poreč").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) They were later joined by Petko Katrandžijev "Mlinac" (keyboards), and Škrinjarić was replaced by Radovan Krajnović.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)

The band had their debut performance at the prestigious [Zagreb Music Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Music_Institute "Croatian Music Institute").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-istorija109-2) During the following years, they would continue to occasionally perform there, although they played mostly in Zagreb clubs Medicinar (_Medicine Student_) and Ribnjak (_Fish Pond_).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) They played almost exclusively covers of songs by American rock and roll artists, like [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), [Bo Diddley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Diddley "Bo Diddley") and [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry"), in which they differed from other Yugoslav bands of the early 1960s, as other Yugoslav groups of the era often performed covers of popular [schlagers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlagers "Schlagers").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Bezimeni also performed covers of [instrumental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumental_rock "Instrumental rock") songs by [Johnny and the Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_and_the_Hurricanes "Johnny and the Hurricanes").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) The band had one appearance in the [Television Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrvatska_radiotelevizija "Hrvatska radiotelevizija")[children's show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_television_series "Children's television series")_Slavica i Mendo_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-istorija109-2) After spending the summer of 1964 performing in [Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadar "Zadar"),

Bezimeni ended their activity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
After Bezimeni disbanded, Mlinarić, Rački and Krajnović moved to the band [Bijele Strijele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bijele_Strijele "Bijele Strijele").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Milnarić later performed as a member of [Karlo Metikoš](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlo_Metiko%C5%A1?action=edit&redlink=1 "Karlo Metikoš (page does not exist)")'s backing band and in 1978 founded his Trooly Studio and started a career in music production.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
Ismailovski performed with the band Kennedy Boys, later moving abroad.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Upon his return to Zagreb, he started a [café](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9 "Café") and performed with the band Cadillac.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)

Katrandžijev performed with Kennedy Boys and [Delfini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfini_(Zagreb_band) "Delfini (Zagreb band)"), later starting a successful career as [pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") composer and producer.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) His most prominent works include the songs for the popular band [Indexi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indexi "Indexi").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) In 2018, [Croatia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Records "Croatia Records") released a compilation of his songs composed for different artists entitled _Gold Collection_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) For his 2019 album _Francais – Electric Piano_ he recorded [classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music") pieces.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) He died on 20 April 2015.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3)
Škrinjarić lost his life in 1968 in an accident in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3) Margetić died in 2000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3)

Bezimeni reunited in 2002, performing on the celebration of [Croatian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") national [skiing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skiing "Skiing") team's success.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3) The reunited Bezimeni entered the recording studio for the first time, making recordings of their old song "Shadoogie", "Crossfire" and "Revival".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3) The songs were published on the [box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_set "Box set")_Kad je rock bio mlad - Priče sa istočne strane (1956-1970)_ (_When Rock Was Young - East Side Stories (1956-1970)_), released by [Croatia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Records "Croatia Records") in 2005 and featuring songs by the pioneering Yugoslav rock acts.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3)

**By Nick Warburton**
**The Tridents 1962**
*   **John Lucas – rhythm guitar**  
*   **Paul Lucas – bass**  
*   **Andrew Baxter – lead guitar**  
*   **Dave Niblett – drums**
**Chiswick band The Tridents were formed in 1961 and are best known for containing Jeff Beck in their ranks from late August 1964-early March 1965.**
**This feature includes a recording of Tiger in your Tank’ performed by Jeff Beck lead guitar, Paul Lucas vocals and bass guitar, John Lucas on rhythm guitar and Ray Cook on drums in 1964. It is the first time any of this material has been released in any form.**
[![Image 1: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/The-Tridents-A-1024x762.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/the-tridents-a)
_The Tridents,1962. Barry Bunting vocals,Paul Lucas bass guitar,Dave Niblett drums,John Lucas rhythm guitar,Andrew Baxter lead guitar_
The original formation (with the above line-up) was put together as an instrumental outfit, and played regularly at the Cavendish School Youth Club in Chiswick alongside The Detours with Roger Daltry on lead guitar and vocals.
According to the Lucas brothers, the original quartet did an audition for the BBC at the BBC Theatre, thanks to Dave Niblett’s connections with the floor manager. Unfortunately, nothing came from the audition because the BBC wanted a band that wrote its own material.
[![Image 2: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/25jan64x-1024x762.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/25jan64x)
_The Tridents, Bennett Street Club, Chiswick, 25 January 1964. Left to right: Leslie Jones, Lindsay Bex, John Lucas and Paul Lucas. Photographer: Janet Croucher_

Not long after, singer Barry Bunting fronted the band for a very brief period but did not stay long. Around this time, in early 1962, The Tridents were offered some gigs in Germany after entertaining some exchange students at St Thomas’s School in Chiswick, but Andrew Baxter was unable to go due to health concerns and so the musicians declined the offer.
[![Image 3: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/25jan64xxx.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/25jan64xxx)
_John Lucas (left) and Paul Lucas (right), Bennett Street Club, Chiswick, 25 January 1964. Photographer: Janet Croucher_
Pete Hammerton, who went on to play lead guitar with The Others and Sands, claims that he played with The Tridents before the German offer. However, both Lucas brothers have no recollection of Hammerton’s involvement. They did, however, rehearse with a guitarist but he never gigged with the band from what they recall. By this point, the Lucas brothers handled lead vocals between them.
Soon after, Ken Lawrence took over the drum stool from Dave Niblett. Ken went on to play in Four Plus One/The In Crowd with Keih West, Steve Howe and John Woods. This soul-rock band later morphed into psychedelic pioneers Tomorrow.
Then, in October 1963, Leslie Jones took over lead guitar in The Tridents from Andrew Baxter.They soon became regulars at Arthur Chisnall’s Eel Pie Island and the Ealing Club,building up quite a reputation.
Notable gigs:
30 November 1963 – Kew Boathouse, Kew, Surrey
10 January 1964 – Ealing Club, Ealing, Middlesex
13 January 1964 – Flamingo, Soho
Around early January 1964, The Tridents signed up with The Rik Gunnell Agency. On 16 January, Lindsay Bex, who’d previously played with Mike Forde & The Fortunes, took over on drums.

[![Image 4: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/25jan64xx.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/25jan64xx)
_The Tridents, left to right: Lindsay Bex, Leslie Jones, John Lucas and Paul Lucas, Bennett Street Club, Chiswick,25 January 1964. Photographer: Janet Croucher_

According to the Lucas brothers, the band came across Ray Cook at an open-air gig at Argyle Park in Ealing during June 1964. An inspirational, 16-year-old drummer, who was transported to gigs by his father in an American shooting brake (estate car with wood panels like the old Morris Minor estate), Ray Cook impressed the brothers so much that they decided to dispense with Lindsay Bex after the mini-tour of the south coast. Ray Cook remained with the band until 28 May 1965 when the group disbanded.
However, Bex’s diary confirms that he played his final gig on 4 July. The drummer would later go on to play with The Magic Roundabout. It is possible that Cook played his first gig on 4 July (later that evening) but most likely it is the Eel Pie Island gig four days later.

In the early 1960s, the band gained popularity with their live performances on which they covered [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_America "United States of America")[rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") hits. The group disbanded in 1964, reuniting 36 years later for a live performance, recording several of their 1960s songs for the first time.
Bezimeni were formed in 1961 by [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb "Zagreb") high school students Janko Mlinarić "Truli" (vocals, bass guitar), Slaven Rački (guitar), Željko Margetić "Marga" (guitar), Mahmud Ismailovski "Mamut" (tenor saxophone) and Mario Škrinjarić (drums).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) The five made an agreement to form the band during a school excursion to [Poreč](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pore%C4%8D "Poreč").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) They were later joined by Petko Katrandžijev "Mlinac" (keyboards), and Škrinjarić was replaced by Radovan Krajnović.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
texts.2: The band had their debut performance at the prestigious [Zagreb Music Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Music_Institute "Croatian Music Institute").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-istorija109-2) During the following years, they would continue to occasionally perform there, although they played mostly in Zagreb clubs Medicinar (_Medicine Student_) and Ribnjak (_Fish Pond_).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) They played almost exclusively covers of songs by American rock and roll artists, like [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), [Bo Diddley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Diddley "Bo Diddley") and [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry"), in which they differed from other Yugoslav bands of the early 1960s, as other Yugoslav groups of the era often performed covers of popular [schlagers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlagers "Schlagers").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Bezimeni also performed covers of [instrumental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumental_rock "Instrumental rock") songs by [Johnny and the Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_and_the_Hurricanes "Johnny and the Hurricanes").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) The band had one appearance in the [Television Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrvatska_radiotelevizija "Hrvatska radiotelevizija")[children's show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_television_series "Children's television series")_Slavica i Mendo_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-istorija109-2) After spending the summer of 1964 performing in [Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadar "Zadar"),
texts.3:
Bezimeni ended their activity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
After Bezimeni disbanded, Mlinarić, Rački and Krajnović moved to the band [Bijele Strijele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bijele_Strijele "Bijele Strijele").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Milnarić later performed as a member of [Karlo Metikoš](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlo_Metiko%C5%A1?action=edit&redlink=1 "Karlo Metikoš (page does not exist)")'s backing band and in 1978 founded his Trooly Studio and started a career in music production.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
Ismailovski performed with the band Kennedy Boys, later moving abroad.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) Upon his return to Zagreb, he started a [café](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9 "Café") and performed with the band Cadillac.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1)
texts.4:
Katrandžijev performed with Kennedy Boys and [Delfini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfini_(Zagreb_band) "Delfini (Zagreb band)"), later starting a successful career as [pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") composer and producer.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) His most prominent works include the songs for the popular band [Indexi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indexi "Indexi").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) In 2018, [Croatia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Records "Croatia Records") released a compilation of his songs composed for different artists entitled _Gold Collection_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) For his 2019 album _Francais – Electric Piano_ he recorded [classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music") pieces.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8735-1) He died on 20 April 2015.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3)
Škrinjarić lost his life in 1968 in an accident in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3) Margetić died in 2000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezimeni#cite_note-janjatovi%C4%8736-3)

**By Nick Warburton**
**The Tridents 1962**
*   **John Lucas – rhythm guitar**  
*   **Paul Lucas – bass**  
*   **Andrew Baxter – lead guitar**  
*   **Dave Niblett – drums**
**Chiswick band The Tridents were formed in 1961 and are best known for containing Jeff Beck in their ranks from late August 1964-early March 1965.**
**This feature includes a recording of Tiger in your Tank’ performed by Jeff Beck lead guitar, Paul Lucas vocals and bass guitar, John Lucas on rhythm guitar and Ray Cook on drums in 1964. It is the first time any of this material has been released in any form.**
[![Image 1: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/The-Tridents-A-1024x762.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/the-tridents-a)
_The Tridents,1962. Barry Bunting vocals,Paul Lucas bass guitar,Dave Niblett drums,John Lucas rhythm guitar,Andrew Baxter lead guitar_
The original formation (with the above line-up) was put together as an instrumental outfit, and played regularly at the Cavendish School Youth Club in Chiswick alongside The Detours with Roger Daltry on lead guitar and vocals.
According to the Lucas brothers, the original quartet did an audition for the BBC at the BBC Theatre, thanks to Dave Niblett’s connections with the floor manager. Unfortunately, nothing came from the audition because the BBC wanted a band that wrote its own material.
[![Image 2: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/25jan64x-1024x762.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/25jan64x)
_The Tridents, Bennett Street Club, Chiswick, 25 January 1964. Left to right: Leslie Jones, Lindsay Bex, John Lucas and Paul Lucas. Photographer: Janet Croucher_
texts.1:
Not long after, singer Barry Bunting fronted the band for a very brief period but did not stay long. Around this time, in early 1962, The Tridents were offered some gigs in Germany after entertaining some exchange students at St Thomas’s School in Chiswick, but Andrew Baxter was unable to go due to health concerns and so the musicians declined the offer.
[![Image 3: The Tridents](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/25jan64xxx.jpg)](https://thestrangebrew.co.uk/articles/the-tridents/25jan64xxx)
_John Lucas (left) and Paul Lucas (right), Bennett Street Club, Chiswick, 25 January 1964. Photographer: Janet Croucher_
Pete Hammerton, who went on to play lead guitar with The Others and Sands, claims that he played with The Tridents before the German offer. However, both Lucas brothers have no recollection of Hammerton’s involvement. They did, however, rehearse with a guitarist but he never gigged with the band from what they recall. By this point, the Lucas brothers handled lead vocals between them.
Soon after, Ken Lawrence took over the drum stool from Dave Niblett. Ken went on to play in Four Plus One/The In Crowd with Keih West, Steve Howe and John Woods. This soul-rock band later morphed into psychedelic pioneers Tomorrow.
Then, in October 1963, Leslie Jones took over lead guitar in The Tridents from Andrew Baxter.They soon became regulars at Arthur Chisnall’s Eel Pie Island and the Ealing Club,building up quite a reputation.
Notable gigs:
30 November 1963 – Kew Boathouse, Kew, Surrey
10 January 1964 – Ealing Club, Ealing, Middlesex
13 January 1964 – Flamingo, Soho
Around early January 1964, The Tridents signed up with The Rik Gunnell Agency. On 16 January, Lindsay Bex, who’d previously played with Mike Forde & The Fortunes, took over on drums.

According to the Lucas brothers, the band came across Ray Cook at an open-air gig at Argyle Park in Ealing during June 1964. An inspirational, 16-year-old drummer, who was transported to gigs by his father in an American shooting brake (estate car with wood panels like the old Morris Minor estate), Ray Cook impressed the brothers so much that they decided to dispense with Lindsay Bex after the mini-tour of the south coast. Ray Cook remained with the band until 28 May 1965 when the group disbanded.
However, Bex’s diary confirms that he played his final gig on 4 July. The drummer would later go on to play with The Magic Roundabout. It is possible that Cook played his first gig on 4 July (later that evening) but most likely it is the Eel Pie Island gig four days later.
